exposure: Number of prior cesarean sections (1, 2, 3 or more)
History of Cesarean Section vs. No History of Cesarean Section
outcome: Intraoperative and postoperative complication rates (blood transfusions, conversion to laparotomy, vascular or visceral injury, surgical site complications, emergency room visits)
cohort: 484 patients who underwent laparoscopic hysterectomy by a minimally invasive gynecologic surgery (MIGS) fellowship-trained surgeon at a single tertiary care center in the southeastern United States from 2016 to 2019.
finding: Neither a history of any cesarean section nor the total number of prior cesarean sections significantly affected estimated blood loss, operative time, or intraoperative or postoperative complications of laparoscopic hysterectomies performed by MIGS-trained surgeons.
